_README: CONTRACT for the channel-evidence layer (RUNBOOK-77/78). This file is the knob the
intranet edits; retriever/channel_evidence.py should not need editing when the box's
generator changes its field names, adds a channel, or reorders the evidence hierarchy.
Two DIFFERENT files feed this layer, and the difference is load-bearing:
evidence_file  — what was FOUND. Per repo: which channels, on what basis, with a citation.
scope_file     — what was LOOKED AT. Without it, 'no evidence' is ambiguous: the engine
cannot tell 'scanned and genuinely clean' from 'never scanned', and it
will say so out loud rather than pick the flattering reading.
The reader accepts three evidence shapes so a generator change never needs an engine
field_aliases lets the box keep its own column names. Matching ignores case, spaces,
underscores and hyphens, so 'citation', 'Citation' and 'cite_ref' all resolve if listed.
Any value outside the enums below is DROPPED with a counted reason, never coerced into
something plausible — an invented channel is worse than a missing one.
_relation_order_README: Strongest evidence first. This is the order answers and UI are ranked by, and it is data
rather than code so the box can reorder it after seeing real results.
low-confidence direct evidence is DEMOTED to just below message_carried: a weak code hit
(a channel word in a class name, say) is a worse reason to name a channel than a topic
that demonstrably carries it. Set demote_low_confidence to false to rank purely by basis.
transitive_dependency is LAST and is never ownership. It answers 'this would be affected',
_notes_README: The generator's free-text `note` is produced by scanning source, so it can carry code
fragments, vendor identifiers or endpoints. It is therefore NOT returned by default: the
citation is the evidence, and the note is commentary. A caller that wants notes must ask
for them explicitly AND put them through the egress gate that already exists for the
incident line. Flip this to true only after the box has confirmed what notes contain.
